mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the rotating disk was most worthwhile: it connected the cloud’s rotation to material orbiting the protostar rather than falling straight in.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making sunlight by combining the young Sun with open space felt like a predictable goal-completion step rather than a substantial new decision.

surprise.text: Adding hydrogen produced a contracting young Sun, not sustained fusion; planet formation can begin before main-sequence burning.

arbitrary.text: Adding rock-forming dust to the existing dusty disk made sense, but felt somewhat like an extra completion step rather than a clearly distinct physical transition.

continue.text: Yes. I’d be curious to see how the disk’s mixed materials become planets, especially after the clear distinction between early solar light and sustained fusion.
